title: Appliance Rebates in Greater Sudbury 2026: Up to $200 Per Appliance
desc: Greater Sudbury appliance rebates for 2026: $25 to $200 from Home Renovation Savings, with Greater Sudbury Hydro as distributor.
lead: Greater Sudbury has 71,475 households, with January lows averaging -15.2°C. The appliance rebates are the same as everywhere in Ontario.
cards_heading: What Ontario pays for new appliances in Greater Sudbury
cards_intro: We re-read the program's appliance page on October 4, 2026. The rebates are province-wide, so the amounts are the same in every city, and the rules about what you replace and which model you buy are what decide a claim.

cards.title: Heat pump clothes dryer
cards.note: The largest of the six appliance rebates, for a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient heat pump dryer replacing an electric dryer.

cards.title: Induction cooktop or range
cards.note: For a new induction cooktop or range on the program's product list, replacing an existing electric one.

cards.title: Washing machine
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient washer on the program list.

cards.title: Fridge
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient refrigerator replacing an existing electric one.

cards.title: Freezer
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient freezer on the list.

cards.title: Dishwasher
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient dishwasher on the list.

cards.title: Who can claim
cards.note: A residential customer on the Ontario grid with an existing electric appliance in need of replacing. Cornwall Electric customers are excluded.

cards.title: Free route
cards.note: Income-qualified households can get energy-efficient fridges and freezers at no charge, along with other upgrades.

after_cards: The appliance page states no end date, so confirm it is still open before you buy.
sections: A cold city and the laundry room

Sudbury's average January low is -15.2°C. 61% of its households live in detached houses and only 7% in tall buildings. A heat pump dryer pays $200. The program only checks the model and that it replaces an electric dryer; where it goes is a question for the maker and your installer.
Greater Sudbury Hydro is the distributor, and Sudbury postal codes begin with P, which the Energy Affordability Program lists. 36% of households rent.

The program page asks for an existing electric appliance in need of replacing. A new fridge to go in a spare corner, or an induction range where the kitchen had no range, is not a replacement. If you are switching from gas to an electric appliance, the page does not say whether that counts, so ask the program before you buy. Greater Sudbury households that already cook on an electric range are the clearest fit for the induction rebate.
Fridges and freezers at no cost

The Energy Affordability Program lists energy-efficient refrigerators and freezers among the items that comprehensive support can provide, along with LED bulbs, dehumidifiers and window air conditioners. It does not list washers or dryers, and its saving kits include no major appliances. Income limits run from $48,220 for one person to $96,439 for four, and Greater Sudbury postal codes are among those it covers. Call 1-844-770-3148 to ask.

The page states no limit per household and no end date. That does not mean unlimited funding, and the program can change. If you plan to replace a washer and a dryer, or a fridge and a freezer, get them on the program's lists first and keep every receipt, since each claim is separate and has its own 60-day window.
Most Efficient, not just ENERGY STAR

The rebate is for ENERGY STAR Most Efficient models, which the page describes as going beyond standard ENERGY STAR requirements. A fridge with the ordinary ENERGY STAR mark may not qualify. Each appliance has its own product list linked from the program page, so find the model number there before you pay, whether you buy in Greater Sudbury or online.
claim_heading: How to claim in Greater Sudbury
claim_steps: Check that the appliance you are replacing is electric and that you are on the Ontario grid.
Find a new model on the program's ENERGY STAR Most Efficient list for that appliance.
Buy it new from any retailer and keep the receipt.
Upload the receipt on the program page within 60 days of purchase.
If your household income is under the limits, call 1-844-770-3148 about free fridges and freezers first.
faq: Does Greater Sudbury Hydro give an appliance rebate?
What if I heat with oil?
The appliance rebate does not depend on heating fuel, only on replacing an electric appliance and being on the Ontario grid.
Yes, if household income is under the limit, through the Energy Affordability Program.
